CweFindings.Name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.
CweFindings.Explanation: UploadAsync assigns Request.Files.Count directly to fileCount and loops until that client-controlled count is exhausted. No application-level cap limits the per-request iteration or resulting blob uploads.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Initialization
CweFindings.Description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.
CweFindings.Explanation: The static blobContainer is initialized only inside Index (lines 65-66), but UploadAsync, DeleteImage, and DeleteAll use it without ensuring Index has run. Direct requests to those actions before Index leave the resource null and cause operation failures.

CweFindings.Name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.blobContainer is a static field shared across concurrent MVC requests. Index assigns it while UploadAsync and other actions read it, with no synchronization or safe initialization, so requests can observe an inconsistent lifecycle state.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
CweFindings.Description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.Index creates the blob container with PublicAccessType.Blob, granting anonymous public read access to blob contents. This permission is broader than an access-controlled photo gallery resource.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: UploadAsync, DeleteImage, and DeleteAll perform security-relevant storage changes, but their exception handlers only copy exception text/stack trace into ViewData and do not record upload or deletion events in an application log or audit trail.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync accepts every item in Request.Files without checking its extension or content type and uploads it to the blob container using the submitted filename extension. The container is initialized with public blob access in HomeController.Index (line 66), allowing arbitrary uploaded content to be served publicly without a file-type restriction.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: DisplayFilesToUpload concatenates the browser-supplied file.name directly into an HTML string, then assigns that string to FilesToUpload.innerHTML. A specially named local file can therefore inject markup or script into the page when the user selects it.
